items.title: Open-channel admissions will not affect public university quotas, says Zambry
items.summary: Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said open-channel admissions accounted for only a small percentage of intake and were limited to courses with available places, rather than being driven solely by revenue considerations. Meanwhile, Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing said Malaysia recorded 32.26 million international visitor arrivals from January to September this year, a 2.4 per cent increase from the same period last year. To improve international connectivity, Tiong said Tourism Malaysia had partnered 24 airlines – three domestic and 21 international – to support 46 international routes from January to October this year.

items.title: Tiger sightings spark fear among 500 Kuala Krai villagers
items.summary: KUALA KRAI: About 500 residents in four villages in Mukim Sungai Mengkuang are living in fear after a tiger was spotted near a forest in the area more than two weeks ago. The affected villages are Kampung Nara, Kampung Bukit Pacat, Kampung Gajah Mati and Kampung Slow Temiang. Another rubber tapper, Sukarman Ibrahim, 59, said he found fresh tiger footprints along the path to his plantation about two weeks ago.

items.title: Zahari backs BN's Durian Tunggal candidate despite being dropped
items.summary: Zahari said he was not disappointed with the party's decision to field another candidate, and remained committed to Umno and BN and the people of Durian Tunggal. He said he had continued meeting residents since the candidates were announced and would support Mustafa, better known as Cikgu Mus, if he won the seat. he said while meeting residents with Mustafa at Kampung Belimbing Dalam, Durian Tunggal, today.

items.title: Special delivery? Man nabbed over cannabis and drug-laced vapes at Kelantan courier outlet
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Oct 28 — The General Operations Force (GOF) arrested a man, 30, in the parking lot of the Rantau Panjang Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security (ICQS) Complex early yesterday to assist investigations into a drug seizure at a courier premises in Rantau Panjang, Pasir Mas, on Sunday. GOF Tenggara Brigade Commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the suspect is believed to be linked to the seizure of three kilogrammes of cannabis, 56 grammes of cannabis flowers and 10 boxes of electronic cigarettes containing cannabis oil at a Line Clear Express courier premises. The suspect also pointed out a silver Toyota Camry believed to be used for illicit activities located five metres from where he was arrested and claimed that he was contacted by an individual to help send packages to the courier premises.

items.title: Bursa Malaysia opens higher on improved sentiment
items.summary: The benchmark index opened 2.64 points higher at 1,614.49. Among the heavyweight stocks, Maybank rose one sen to RM10.00, while CIMB added two sen to RM7.13. VS Industry, MYMBN and Dagang Nexchange added one sen each to 35.5 sen, 17.5 sen and 45 sen, respectively.

items.title: Kedah Fire Dept says ‘Bomba’ vehicle allegedly caught running red light is not its own
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Oct 28 — The Kedah Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) has confirmed that a private vehicle bearing the word “Bomba” and equipped with a beacon light is neither an official department vehicle nor one belonging to any Volunteer Fire Brigade (PBS) in the state. “The Kedah JBPM takes a serious view of any unauthorised use of the department’s identity, which could mislead the public and undermine the image and credibility of the fire service,” the statement said. The department also urged the public not to speculate or disseminate unverified information that could cause confusion.

items.title: Kee Ming earnings set to jump on data centre, solar projects
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Kee Ming Group Bhd is expected to post stronger earnings of RM7 million to RM9 million in the second quarter of the financial year 2027 (Q2 FY27), up 16 to 40 per cent quarter-on-quarter (QoQ). Maybank Investment Bank Bhd (Maybank IB) said the earnings growth would be driven by progress in its data centre electrical fit-out and solar interconnection facility (IF) projects. The projected earnings of RM7 million to RM9 million would be higher than the RM6.4 million recorded in Q1 FY27.

items.title: Nestle Malaysia rides demand recovery, secures higher earnings forecasts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Nestle (Malaysia) Bhd is expected to sustain earnings growth in the fourth quarter of 2026, supported by resilient demand and improving cost efficiencies, says CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd. Analyst Walter Aw Lik Hsin said improving cost efficiencies and operating leverage should help cushion higher input costs, although earnings could moderate quarter-on-quarter due to a higher cost base. He said government cash assistance under the 2027 Budget, particularly Sumbangan Asas Rahmah and Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah, should support household purchasing power and demand for Nestle Malaysia's products.

items.title: Don’t just use technology, create it: Malaysia must step up innovation drive, says Mosti
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — Malaysia must accelerate and strengthen its science, technology and innovation (STI) efforts to move beyond being a technology user and become a developer and commercialiser of homegrown technologies, said Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk Chang Lih Kang. Chang said this required a whole-of-nation approach, with close cooperation between the federal and state governments to strengthen the STI ecosystem, develop local talent and expand technology adoption based on each state’s needs and economic potential. Chang said MEXCO-STI provided an important platform to align policies, strategies and implementation of the national STI agenda between the federal and state governments.

items.title: Missing 14-year-old boy attacked by crocodile found dead
items.summary: SEBUYAU: A 14-year-old boy who was reported missing after being attacked by a crocodile in Ulu Sungai Plaie was found dead about 800m from the Kampung Tuba jetty at 8pm yesterday. The victim, Mohd Nordin Mohd Othman, was found with several body parts missing. The villager was returning home after visiting the victim's family in Kampung Plaie when he saw the crocodile.

items.title: Putrajaya still working on loophole in planned road crash payouts: What if offenders have no money?
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — Bereaved families who lose a breadwinner to reckless or drunk drivers could soon secure direct compensation through criminal courts, but the federal government is still working out how awards will be collected if the convicted motorist possesses no financial means. The Transport Ministry is preparing amendments to the Road Transport Act 1987 to establish a statutory compensation framework for victims and lawful heirs in road crashes resulting in death or grievous hurt, according to a written parliamentary reply tabled in the Dewan Rakyat. Kadir, the ministry said that Putrajaya favours judicial discretion over fixed administrative payout caps.

items.title: Kuching North achieves Level 1 Smart City status, now sets sights on Level 2
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 28 — Kuching North has achieved Smart City Level 1 under the Smart City Rating Criteria set by the Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT), with efforts now geared towards meeting the requirements for Level 2. Caretaker Minister in the Premier’s Department Datuk Dr Abdul Rahman Junaidi said the achievement reflected Kuching North City Commission’s (DBKU) continued efforts to strengthen urban governance through technology and innovation. Among the smart city initiatives implemented by DBKU are smart street lighting, smart traffic lights, Geographic Information System, and closed-circuit television systems.

items.title: 3 arrested after Alza drives against traffic to evade police in Johor
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI: Three men were arrested and another is being sought after they allegedly drove against traffic on the Second Link Expressway to evade a police check. Iskandar Puteri district police chief Assistant Commissioner Radin Ramlan Radin Taha said the three suspects comprised a Malaysian and two Filipinos. Police arrested three suspects, while the fourth remains at large, Radin Ramlan said.

items.title: Life after the military: Nearly 800 veterans find new careers beyond the uniform through Kerjaya Kedua Perwira initiative, says Khaled
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — A total of 1,409 prospective retirees and veterans of the Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) have benefited from the Kerjaya Kedua Perwira initiative under the Perhebat Transformation Plan as of September, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said. “Meanwhile, 628 prospective MAF retirees are undergoing industry-based training,” he said at the 71st Convocation Ceremony of the Armed Forces Ex-Servicemen Affairs Corporation (Perhebat) at Dewan Jubli Perak, Perhebat Complex, Sungai Buloh Camp, near here, yesterday. Mohamed Khaled said Perhebat must remain proactive in enhancing the skills, competencies and employability of service personnel and veterans to enable them to pursue high-value career opportunities.

items.title: Driver killed after car hits wild boar, crashes into lorry
items.summary: HULU SELANGOR: A driver was killed after his car hit a wild boar, swerved and crashed into a lorry near a petrol station in Kalumpang. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said a team from the Kuala Kubu Baru Fire and Rescue Station was deployed to the scene. Firefighters initially found the driver trapped in the vehicle and unconscious.

items.title: Man to face charges over ramming GOF vehicle during police pursuit
items.summary: PASIR MAS: A 35-year-old man is expected to face three charges at the Pasir Mas magistrate's court today after ramming a General Operations Force (GOF) vehicle during a police pursuit. He is expected to be charged under Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987, Section 12(2) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 and Section 186 of the Penal Code. On Oct 24, the suspect allegedly rammed a four-wheel-drive vehicle carrying four GOF personnel during a pursuit along Jalan Pekan Lama, Rantau Panjang.

items.title: What went wrong at sea? MMEA to review SOPs after fatal Perlis boat pursuit
items.summary: KUALA NERANG, Oct 28 — The Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) will conduct an internal investigation into a boat collision that claimed the life of one of its personnel in waters off Perlis two days ago. MMEA Deputy Director-General (Operations) Maritime Vice-Admiral Mohd Zawawi Abdullah said the investigation would focus on identifying weaknesses and determining whether the agency’s standard operating procedures (SOPs) needed improvement to prevent similar incidents. Mohd Zawawi said the investigation would also examine other areas for improvement, including personnel training and the equipment used during operations.

items.title: Pay-as-you-drive insurance being studied to lower costs for e-hailing drivers, Transport Ministry says
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The federal government is studying dynamic insurance and takaful models that price coverage based on mileage and driver risk profiles, seeking to rein in escalating vehicle operating costs across the e-hailing industry. In a written reply yesterday to Bakri MP Tan Hong Pin in the Dewan Rakyat, the Transport Ministry confirmed that a dedicated Inter-Agency Task Force (IATF) convened by Bank Negara Malaysia is spearheading efforts to restructure e-hailing insurance mechanisms and alleviate the financial burden on drivers. The long-term reform brings together the Transport Ministry, Bank Negara, the Land Public Transport Agency (APAD), the Road Transport Department (JPJ), insurance and takaful providers, and e-hailing driver associations under a coordinated inter-agency framework.

items.title: 2,097 police personnel arrested for drugs, robbery, corruption since 2021
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 2,097 police personnel and officers were arrested for drug, robbery and corruption offences from 2021 to August this year. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said of these, 1,551 were arrested for drug offences, 64 for robbery and 482 by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC). In a written parliamentary reply to Lim Lip Eng (PH-Kepong), who asked for the number of police personnel arrested for the offences since 2021, Saifuddin provided a yearly breakdown.

items.title: A father’s final farewell: Jalur Gemilang presented as MMEA officer killed at sea laid to rest in Kedah
items.summary: KUALA NERANG, Oct 28 — The remains of Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) officer Technical Leading Seaman Mohd Roshaimi Mohd Ridzuan, 41, who died in a boat collision in Perlis waters yesterday, were laid to rest last night. After the funeral, MMEA deputy director-general (Operations) Vice-Admiral (Maritime) Mohd Zawawi Abdullah presented the Jalur Gemilang to the deceased’s father. Also present were Kedah and Perlis MMEA director First Admiral (Maritime) Romli Mustafa and dozens of MMEA personnel.

items.title: JCorp hits back at Indonesian forest fire claims, says plantation ties ended years ago
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 28 — Johor Corporation (JCorp) yesterday refuted claims associating the group with Indonesian plantation companies linked to forest and land fires, following a recent report published by Wahana Linkungan Hidup Indonesia (WALHI). JCorp further explained that through its wholly owned subsidiary, Kulim (Malaysia) Berhad (Kulim), it divested its interests in several Indonesian companies in 2007. The disposals involved PT Graha Cakra Mulia, PT Sumber Mahardhika Graha, PT Salonok Ladang Mas, and PT Harapan Hibrida Kalbar on August 8, 2007, followed by PT Trimurti Sumbertama on September 26, 2007, with all disposals recorded in JCorp’s 2008 Annual Report.

items.title: Bukit Aman CID takes over custodial death probe after forensic examination reveals blunt-force injuries
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The investigation into the death of Noorizwan Zulkefly while in police custody has been taken over by the Prosecution/Legal Division (D5) of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) at Bukit Aman. Bukit Aman CID director Datuk M. Kumar said the case is now being investigated under Section 331 of the Penal Code, on intentional infliction of grievous hurt to extort a confession or to compel the restoration of property. Kumar added that the investigation is ongoing to identify the police officers and personnel involved in the handling and management of the victim while he was in custody at Cheras district police headquarters.

items.title: MMEA to probe fatal boat collision off Perlis
items.summary: KUALA NERANG: The Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) will conduct an internal investigation into a boat collision that killed its sailor off Perlis on Monday night. MMEA deputy director-general (Operations) Maritime Vice-Admiral Mohd Zawawi Abdullah said the investigation would identify shortcomings and determine whether standard operating procedures (SOPs) needed to be improved to prevent similar incidents. Zawawi said the investigation would also examine the training and operational equipment.

items.title: ‘Corporate Mafia’ probe freezes over RM400m in assets, no MACC officers implicated, Home Ministry tells Parliament
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — Federal police have found no evidence linking Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) officers to alleged “corporate mafia” syndicates after questioning 70 individuals in an ongoing anti-money laundering operation, the Home Ministry told the Dewan Rakyat. “At present, the Op Viking investigation is continuing in order to complete the entire investigation paper. In response, the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) launched Op Viking through its specialized Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA) criminal investigation division, opening formal investigation papers on Oct 14, 2025, under Section 4(1) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001.

items.title: WCE heading south? Zahid says Banting-Masjid Tanah extension a priority, Johor next on the cards
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Oct 28 — The extension of the West Coast Expressway (WCE) from Banting, Selangor, to Masjid Tanah was among the matters discussed by the Cabinet, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. Moving forward, God willing, the route from Banting to Masjid Tanah, continuing toward Batu Pahat and Pontian, will pass through Masjid Tanah. We will prioritise the section from Masjid Tanah to Banting, God willing,” he said.

items.title: Open-channel admissions won’t reduce UPU quotas at public universities, says Zambry
items.summary: “The government provides various forms of financial support covering tuition fees and living allowances, including the Community College Student Financial Assistance, Foundation Financial Assistance and B40 TVET Scholarships,” he said. Meanwhile, Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing, when winding up the debate for his ministry, said Malaysia recorded 32.26 million international visitor arrivals from January to September 2026, an increase of 2.4 per cent compared with the same period last year. Tiong said that, to improve international connectivity, Tourism Malaysia had worked with 24 airlines, comprising three domestic and 21 international carriers, to support 46 international flight routes from January to October this year.

items.title: Tiger on the prowl? Suspected paw prints found near Gerik homes, Perhilitan trap activated
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 28 — The Perak Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) has confirmed the discovery of footprints believed to belong to a tiger at Felda Lepang Nenering in Pengkalan Hulu, Gerik, on October 26. Perak Perhilitan director Dr Pazil Abdul Patah said the confirmation was made following an investigation and field inspection by the Gerik District Perhilitan Office after it received a report from a plantation worker about the incident on the same day. “For now, Perhilitan has activated a tiger trap located less than a kilometre from where the footprints were found.

items.title: GOF arrests 55 suspected human smugglers in Kelantan
items.summary: KOTA BARU: The General Operations Force (GOF) has arrested 55 suspected tekong darat (human smugglers), including six women, allegedly behind migrant smuggling along the Kelantan border since last year. GOF Southeast Brigade commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said 35 were arrested last year and another 20 this year. Radzi said integrated operations along the border would be intensified to curb human smuggling, as syndicates were becoming increasingly brazen and had allegedly threatened villagers.

items.title: Kedah fire dept: 'Bomba' vehicle in viral video is not ours
items.summary: ALOR STAR: The Kedah Fire and Rescue Department has confirmed that a private vehicle bearing the word "Bomba" and fitted with a beacon light does not belong to the department or any Volunteer Fire Brigade in the state. In a statement today, the department said it was aware of a video circulating on social media showing the vehicle and was taking further action over the unauthorised use of its identity. "We take a serious view of any unauthorised use of the department's identity, which could mislead the public and undermine the image and credibility of the fire service," it said.

items.title: US costs of Iran war rise to over US$47bil
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The US military has spent more than US$47 billion so far to prosecute the war in Iran, more than 25 per cent higher than the Defence Department's estimate in July, according to Pentagon data obtained by Reuters. The Pentagon's latest estimate was tied to the operational costs of carrying out the war, with a projected cost of more than US$29 billion to replace expended munitions used in the conflict. Trump launched the Iran war jointly with Israel in February, predicting that the conflict would last a short time.

items.title: Melaka polls: Pakatan eyes more seats beyond defending incumbents, says Fahmi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) aims to retain its existing seats and targets to wrest potentially winnable seats in the Melaka state election, said PH communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. The communications minister said the matter was among those discussed at the PH presidential council meeting held yesterday evening to fine-tune preparations for the coalition’s election machinery. On preparations by the election machinery, Fahmi said the Presidential Council had been briefed by Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari and Melaka PKR State Leadership Council (MPN) acting chairman Adam Adli Abdul Halim on the state-level readiness.

items.title: Melaka polls: Ab Rauf claims progress in MCA seat talks despite Wee Ka Siong’s reservations
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Oct 28 — Discussions between Melaka Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh and MCA President Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong is believed to have successfully resolved several deadlocks regarding seat distribution for the Melaka state election (PRN) next month. Ab Rauf, who is also the Melaka BN election director, described the development as “positive” when met by reporters. We will wait for MCA itself to later perhaps provide the outcome (decision) from the negotiations I discussed with him (MCA president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong) (on Monday) night,” he said.

items.title: Tragic discovery: Body of 14-year-old snatched by crocodile in Sarawak finally found
items.summary: KUCHING, — The body of a teenage boy who was attacked by a crocodile at Ulu Sungai Plaie in Sebuyau was found on Tuesday night. In an update at 10.13pm, the Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department (Bomba) said the 14-year-old’s body was found by villagers. The boy, identified as Mohamad Nordin Mohamad Othman, was attacked by a crocodile on Monday afternoon.

items.title: US new home sales cooled in September as mortgage rates surged
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The sale of new US homes slowed in September, government data showed Tuesday, as surging mortgage rates weighed on homebuyers and affordability worries bite. New home sales were down by 0.6 per cent from August, reaching a seasonally-adjusted annual rate of 676,000 last month, said the Commerce Department. The popular 30-year fixed-rate mortgage averaged 7.03 per cent in late September, Freddie Mac data showed, underscoring voters' affordability concerns as US midterm elections approach next month.

items.title: Melaka polls: Respect Pakatan’s decision to give Bemban seat to Bersatu, Amirudin tells dissenters
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) component parties must respect the coalition’s decision to hand the Bemban state seat to a Bersatu candidate in the Melaka state election, says PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari. Amirudin, who is also Selangor menteri besar, said party members must respect the consensus reached by the coalition and their respective leaderships regarding electoral pacts and seat allocations. On political ties between PH and Bersatu in Selangor, Amirudin said no decision has been reached, pending further deliberations.

items.title: Australia's central bank set to weigh if rate hikes are enough to curb inflation
items.summary: SYDNEY: Australia's central bank will debate whether four rate hikes this year will prove sufficient to return inflation to target at next week's policy meeting, the bank's governor said on Wednesday. Michele Bullock, the governor of the Reserve Bank of Australia told lawmakers oil and related prices had increased sharply again and would add materially to inflation. "A key question is whether the tightening in monetary policy to date will be sufficient to bring inflation back to target in a reasonable time," Bullock added.

items.title: Miti: Malaysia’s exports to US surge 69pc despite tariffs, powered by AI boom
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — Malaysia’s exports to the United States surged 69.1 per cent to RM282.07 billion for January to September 2026, while total trade between the two countries rose 39.6 per cent to RM378.70 billion. The Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (Miti) said Malaysia’s trade performance with the US continues to grow despite its exports being subjected to additional tariffs following investigations under various legal instruments conducted by the US. The ministry noted that the E&E sector accounts for about 64.2 per cent of Malaysia’s total exports to the US, with 44 per cent of E&E exports comprising semiconductor products.

items.title: Trump floats idea of Venezuela becoming '51st state'
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Tuesday suggested that Venezuela could become the 51st US state, citing growing oil cooperation between the two countries, Anadolu Ajansi reported. "I want to thank Venezuela, where our relationship has become very, very good, a great one," Trump told supporters at a midterm election rally in Corpus Christi, Texas. "This historic win gives us control over a massive part of the world's oil supply," he said.

items.title: In Dewan Rakyat today: RM20.1b 1MDB liabilities, BUDI95 quota changes and data centres under spotlight
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The status of efforts to settle 1Malaysia Development Bhd’s (1MDB) remaining net liabilities, estimated at RM20.1 billion, including assets and claims still being recovered, is among the issues expected to be raised in the Dewan Rakyat today. Other issues expected to be raised include data centre operations, plans to upgrade federal and state roads, and measures to address learning loss among pupils from hardcore poor households. Young Syefura Othman (PH-Bentong) is scheduled to ask the works minister about plans to upgrade federal and state roads in Bentong to cope with increased traffic following the completion of the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) project.

items.title: As AI enters classrooms, Anwar warns against losing what makes us human
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — Artificial intelligence (AI) and digital technology are vital for the future of education; however, their use must be balanced with the cultivation of moral, human values, and character among students, said Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. In a video shared on his Facebook page, the prime minister noted that while AI possesses capabilities in terms of knowledge and intelligence, it lacks the values, character, and humanity that must be nurtured within and embodied by human beings. It is merely intelligence,” he said.

items.title: Ringgit opens higher against US dollar for eight consecutive trading days
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar for the eighth consecutive trading day today, reflecting continued positive momentum in the local currency at the start of trading. At 8am, the ringgit rose to 4.0855/0915 against the US dollar from Tuesday's close of 4.0865/0900. The ringgit is expected to hover between RM4.07 and RM4.08 against the US dollar today," he told Bernama.

items.title: Air quality stays healthy nationwide
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Air quality remains at healthy levels nationwide, with no areas recording unhealthy readings. A total of 43 monitoring stations recorded moderate Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 7.50am. Another 25 monitoring stations recorded good air quality.

items.title: Wall Street ends higher on revived AI momentum
items.summary: NEW YORK: An AI-fuelled tech rally sent US stocks to a higher close on Tuesday as third-quarter reporting season gained steam, while the Federal Reserve convened for its penultimate meeting of the year. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index, while off more than 20 per cent from its June 22 record closing high, has outperformed the broader market this year, gaining 62.1 per cent compared with the S&P 500's 12.8 per cent year-to-date advance. Boeing tumbled 10.7 per cent following its bigger-than-expected third-quarter loss, while water-management company Xylem slid 14.2 per cent after trimming full-year forecasts.

items.title: No decision yet on financial aid for debt-hit AirAsia, says Loke
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The government has yet to decide whether to provide financial support to financially distressed AirAsia Group Bhd, said Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook. He said both the Ministry of Transport and the Ministry of Finance are reviewing proposals to assist the airline. “The government’s priority is to ensure ongoing airline operations and maintain connectivity, as the bankruptcy of a major airline would disrupt this connectivity.

items.title: Sarawak seeks more flights and buses to bring voters home for state election
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 28 — The Ministry of Transport Sarawak (MOTS) has written to airlines and express bus operators to explore additional services before and after polling day for the upcoming 13th Sarawak State Election. “For air travel, MOTS has requested airlines to plan for increased flight frequencies during the week before and the week after polling day, to accommodate voters travelling home to vote and their return journeys afterwards. “For express bus services, MOTS has advised and encouraged operators in Sarawak to temporarily increase trip frequencies from three days before polling day until three days after polling day,” according to MOTS.

items.title: #NSTviral: Buffaloes roam Bukit Raja roadside, sparking social media buzz [WATCH]
items.summary: "For those driving near the Bukit Raja area, be careful, there are buffaloes on the loose.," the user wrote. "So many incidents in the Bukit Raja area today, with the floods too," wrote user @tiarasy10. Pity the original inhabitants of the Bukit Rajah estate," the user wrote.

items.title: Climate change must be declared 'global health emergency': Lancet study
items.summary: PARIS: Climate change must be declared a "global health emergency" to shape governments' policies after heat caused three million deaths between 2016 and 2023, a report in The Lancet said Wednesday. And "68 per cent of those deaths are directly attributable to climate change." - Climate change impact - Romanello said the global health emergency due to climate change should have "an integrated approach so that we're not responding to emergency after emergency."

items.title: Ex-cop seeks A-G's intervention over 2015 assault complaint against Shuhaily
items.summary: The move comes a week after Shuhaily was charged with two counts of voluntarily causing hurt to two police personnel at KLIA last month. Lawyers Kamal Hisham Ja'afar and Muhammad Nor Tamrin said their client, Saifuddin Abdul Kader, lodged a police report against Shuhaily on Nov 19, 2015, when the latter was Hilir Perak police chief. "Although a police report was lodged, no action has been taken against Shuhaily to date," they said in a statement today.

items.title: 1MDB liabilities, BUDI95 among issues to be raised in Dewan Rakyat today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The status of efforts to settle 1Malaysia Development Bhd's (1MDB) remaining net liabilities, estimated at RM20.1 billion, including assets and claims still being recovered, is among the issues expected to be raised in the Dewan Rakyat today. Other issues expected to be raised include data centre operations, plans to upgrade federal and state roads, and measures to address learning loss among pupils from hardcore poor households. Meanwhile, Wan Ahmad Fayhsal Wan Ahmad Kamal (PN-Machang) will seek details of the government's contingency plans to ensure that data centre operations do not compromise electricity and water supplies for the public during droughts or supply disruptions.

items.title: 1,600 Lembah Pantai families get RM150 Deepavali vouchers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: About 1,600 families in the Lembah Pantai parliamentary constituency will receive RM150 vouchers in conjunction with Deepavali to help ease their cost of living and cover preparations for the festival. Lembah Pantai Member of Parliament Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the first phase of distribution began yesterday evening, involving more than 300 recipients, while the remaining vouchers would be distributed at several other locations in the constituency tonight. "They can redeem these vouchers at several supermarkets within the Lembah Pantai parliamentary constituency.

items.title: Egypt releases prominent journalist Lina Attalah from custody
items.summary: CAIRO: Egyptian authorities released independent journalist Lina Attalah from custody on Tuesday, hours after she was detained and a court ordered her website shut, her lawyer told AFP. Attalah is one of Egypt's most prominent journalists, and her detention had sparked swift condemnation from rights groups and press freedom advocates. "Lina Attalah was released after we paid the said fine," her lawyer Hassan al-Azhari said, referring to a three million Egyptian pound (US$53,400) fine.

items.title: US says will issue visas to Flavio Bolsonaro, family
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The US State Department will issue visas to defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro and his family, allowing them to enter the US, a senior State Department official said on Tuesday, Anadolu Ajansi reported. The statement came amid reports that Bolsonaro had left Brazil for the United States despite a judicial travel ban. Bolsonaro, who denies any wrongdoing, is reportedly under investigation in cases involving suspected money laundering and currency evasion, as well as the financing of a biographical film about his father, former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro.

items.title: Indian court allows actor Imran Khan to stay until Nov 2
items.summary: MUMBAI: An Indian court has allowed Bollywood actor Imran Khan to remain in the country until at least Nov 2, local media reported on Tuesday, suspending a government order requiring him to leave for allegedly breaching immigration laws by participating in a protest. Khan, 43, is a US citizen and was asked to leave the country by Oct 28 after he was accused of joining protests in Mumbai against the country's election chief this month. Khan appealed against the order in the Bombay High Court, saying it was unconstitutional and arbitrary, local media reported.

items.title: Cyclone Arnab begins making landfall in India's Andhra Pradesh state
items.summary: BHUBANESWAR: A severe cyclone began making landfall in India's Andhra Pradesh state in the early hours of Wednesday, bringing high-speed winds and heavy rain that uprooted trees and disrupted power supplies, authorities said. Thousands of people were evacuated along India's eastern coast this week, and some train and flight services were cancelled ahead of Cyclone Arnab's arrival. No loss of life had been reported so far, although trees had been uprooted in several places and power supplies disrupted, the office of Andhra Pradesh's chief minister said.

items.title: Parliament gets more independence: What will its new council actually do?
items.summary: The law establishes the Parliamentary Service Council to oversee the service, with the aim of strengthening Parliament’s institutional independence from the executive, which refers to the prime minister, Cabinet and government ministries. What is the Parliamentary Service Council? The Parliamentary Service Council is the body responsible for matters relating to the Parliamentary Service, a separate service established under the Parliamentary Service Act 2025 (Act 869).

items.title: Faced with an ageing fleet, Malaysia's fire department turns to robots and upgrades
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) is strengthening its operational and logistical capabilities through asset modernisation efforts and the exploration of new technologies, including Unmanned Remote Systems (URS) involving two Fire Fighting Robots (FFRs). JBPM director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the move was crucial for ensuring the department remained prepared to deal with various emergencies, including fires, accidents, rescue operations and large-scale disasters. He said the replacement of vehicles and equipment would be carried out in stages based on the age and operational capability of existing assets, including the acquisition of 80 Fire Rescue Tenders (FRTs).

items.title: China still tops list of international students in Malaysia, but other markets are growing, says EMGS
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — While China remains Malaysia’s largest source of international students, the Education Malaysia Global Services (EMGS) said applications from other countries are growing. EMGS chairman Datuk Ahmad Shalimin Ahmad Shaffie said China accounted for approximately 41 per cent of applications in 2023, but the proportion has since declined as Malaysia attracts students from more markets. Ahmad Shalimin said regional figures further reflected this growing diversity.

items.title: First the floods, then the heat: MetMalaysia warns of challenging months ahead
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — Malaysia may experience hotter and drier weather towards the end of the 2026/2027 North-east Monsoon (MTL), especially from late January to March next year, following expectations of a Super El Niño phenomenon that could lead to reduced rainfall across the country Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) National Weather and Earthquake Operations Centre senior director Maqrun Fadzli Mohd Fahmi said these conditions could increase the risk of heatwaves and droughts, especially if rainfall decreases during that period. He said the El Niño phenomenon is currently in a strong phase and is expected to intensify to a very strong level or Super El Niño towards the end of this year and into next year. “With reduced rainfall, hot weather or heatwaves often emerge, along with drought due to water shortages caused by insufficient rainfall,” he said as a guest on Bernama TV’s “Fokus 15” programme today.

items.title: Maritime officer killed, three injured during pursuit of suspected migrant boat off Perlis
items.summary: KANGAR, Oct 27 — A Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) personnel was killed and three others injured when their boat collided with a concrete structure during an enforcement operation off Kuala Sungai Padang, Kuala Perlis, last night. Kedah and Perlis Maritime director First Admiral Romli Mustafa said five MMEA personnel were conducting the operation at 11.37pm to intercept a boat suspected of carrying undocumented Myanmar migrants. He said the suspected migrant boat sped towards the shore after being detected, triggering a 15-minute pursuit.

items.title: More than 10,000 visitors expected at National Deepavali celebration in Brickfields on Nov 14
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — More than 10,000 visitors are expected at the National Deepavali Celebration organised by the National Unity Ministry (KPN) in Brickfields here on November 14. Deputy Minister R. Yuneswaran said the event, expected to be officiated by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, would feature arts, culture and heritage activities from morning until night, including performances by artistes and unique exhibitions such as Rumah Malaysia. Yuneswaran called on media practitioners to work with the ministry and relevant departments to promote unity and social harmony, urging them to move away from issues related to the 3Rs (race, religion and royalty) or anything that could undermine social harmony.
